(a) Show each endpoint's own consensus list from consensus_meta.csv (covers 451 of 513 clusters) side by side and label the panel 'consensus per cluster' rather than 'consensus pair' — no new computation, works for any edge whose two clusters both have consensus. (b) Re-run the consensus association step for the 757 cross-module pairs: motif_pair_network/17_consensus_association.py already does this and consensus_presence.npz already holds the 18068x275 and 18068x951 boolean carrier matrices, so co_count and NPMI for any consensus pair are a bitwise AND away. Option (a) for v1, (b) as a build-time job.

gaps.gap: No node-level 2D coordinates anywhere on disk. The only saved embedding (cca_winner_umap.npy) is per protein x UTR PAIR, and averaging its coordinates per node collapses M1/M2/M5/M6 onto each other (centroid separations smaller than within-module std).
gaps.impact: The network view has no reproducible, stable layout out of the box; a naive force simulation will settle differently on every page load, so deep links to 'this region of the graph' and any published-figure resemblance are lost.
gaps.workaround: Run d3-force (or python igraph/networkx) ONCE at build time on the 519-node / 2620-edge graph with a per-module centroid attractor and protein-left / UTR-right bipartite constraint, then ship the frozen (x,y) in nodes.json; let the client optionally re-simulate. Reuse node_select.order_modules() from node_select.py to order the six module blocks by cross-module edge weight (M1-M2 244, M1-M5 192, M2-M3 167 dominate, so a sensible ring order is M5-M1-M2-M3-M4 with M6 hanging off M1).

gaps.gap: No precomputed 6x6 meta-module adjacency file. modules.json records only intra-module n_edges; the inter-module weights that make R3's 'meta modules' view meaningful exist nowhere on disk.
gaps.impact: The top-level meta view (6 supernodes, 15 meta-edges) cannot be rendered from any single existing file.
gaps.workaround: Compute at build time — it is 4 lines of pandas over phylo_corrected_candidates.csv with modules.json. gaps.impact: A user who arrives at the network from R1/R2 with an arbitrary motif will more often than not find that motif's cluster has no place in the meta-module view — a dead end unless handled.

recommendations: Build R3 as three linked levels, all client-side: (1) a 6-supernode meta-graph whose 15 edges are the measured cross-module counts (M1-M2 244, M1-M5 192, M2-M3 167, then a long tail down to 1); (2) the full 519-node / 2,620-edge force graph, which is well within browser limits and needs NO aggregation; (3) a single-module bipartite drill-down (max 133 nodes, M3). Total core payload about 1.5 MB.

Render the network as ONE connected graph, not six. 757 of 2,620 passing edges (28.9%) cross modules, all 15 module pairs are linked, and the giant component is exactly the 513 module-assigned clusters. Six disconnected bipartite panels would misrepresent the data and would erase the manuscript's own M5-protein x M1-UTR observation (98 directed / 192 undirected edges).

Freeze the layout at build time. There are no node-level coordinates on disk, and averaging the pair-UMAP does not separate M1/M2/M5/M6 (centroid gaps smaller than within-module spread). Run d3-force or igraph once with per-module attractors and protein-left / UTR-right constraints, ship the (x,y) in nodes.json, and reuse node_select.order_modules() to order the module blocks by cross-module weight. Keep the pair-UMAP (cca_winner_umap.npy, all 2,620 passing pairs join cleanly) as a separate brush-linked Fig 3c panel.

Design the edge detail panel around partial consensus coverage from the start. Only 1,430 of 2,620 edges (54.6%) have a consensus PAIR, and zero cross-module edges do. Tier it: (a) consensus pair with per-consensus co_count / NPMI / clades where available; (b) otherwise both endpoints' consensus lists from consensus_meta.csv (451 of 513 clusters); (c) otherwise the most frequent literal motif strings from the master parquet. Never show an empty panel.

Put the evidence numbers on every edge, not in a footnote. Each of the 2,620 edges carries n_indep_clades (min 8, median 13, max 23), n_indep_families (median 38), clade_concentration (all below 0.50, mean 0.265) and frac_co_ZNF (max 0.400, only 11 edges above 0.30). A per-edge badge reading 'N independent clades / M families, ZNF fraction X' operationalises the paper's central caveat instead of merely stating it.

Display these caveats verbatim, sourced from the reports. From MODULES_REPORT.md: 'Modules and their GO themes are hypotheses about coordinated protein<->UTR regulatory programs - validate against CLIP/RBP-target, expression co-regulation, and mouse orthologs before treating as established interactions.'; 'Modules depend on the Louvain seed (6 dominant; one of 8 unseeded reruns gave 7) - now seeded.'; 'Module gene sets are broad (1.6-4.3k genes) -> many terms pass q<0.05; read the heatmap / specificity / fold, not the raw count of significant terms.' From REPORT.md: '2,620 of 166,615 co-occurring pairs (1.6 %) pass - these are candidate, unvalidated pairs not explained by single-clade structure, not confirmed interactions.'; 'the ZNF interactions are one clade counted hundreds of times, and crucially they survive p-value-based corrections; only an independent-evidence criterion removes them.'; 'The only honest evidence is the number of independent origins/lineages, and the only true replication is an independent lineage (e.g. mouse orthologs).' From module_gene_members/README.md: 'These are statistical module memberships (motif co-occurrence), not demonstrated physical interactions.'

Add a 'How this network was built' panel quoting the exact gate - clade_concentration < 0.35 AND n_indep_clades >= 8 AND npmi_mip_APC > 0.10 AND co_count >= 10, edge weight = MIp x (1 - clade_concentration) x log1p(n_indep_clades), Louvain modularity 0.47, 9 communities kept down to 6 by requiring >=2 protein motifs / >=2 UTR motifs / >=3 edges. If a threshold slider is offered, state clearly that it re-filters edges but does NOT re-run Louvain, so module assignments stay fixed.

Handle the 43% of clusters with no module explicitly. 387 of 900 clusters (102 prot, 251 utr3, 34 utr5) are absent from every module file, so most motifs a user reaches from R1/R2 will not appear in the network. Give them a first-class 'not assigned to a module' state explaining why, optionally listing their best sub-threshold partners from protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv, clearly marked as below threshold.

Use GO_term_specificity.csv (42 rows, 2.5 KB) for module headlines and comparisons rather than significant-term counts, and default the GO panel to the trusted subset (3,530 of 6,389 rows) with an 'all significant' toggle. This follows the report's own instruction and keeps per-module payloads at 55-335 KB.

Precompute five small build artifacts and keep everything else server-side: nodes.json (513 nodes with module, region, frozen x/y, degree, n_genes, n_instances); edges.json (2,620 edges with the 10 statistical fields plus mp/mu and UMAP x/y); meta_edges.json (15 module pairs with counts and mean scores); consensus.json (top 3 consensus pairs per covered edge, 3,599 rows / 703 KB, plus all of consensus_meta at 156 KB); cluster_labels.json (top 3 informative terms per cluster, extracted from the 13 MB cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz). Never ship module_term_gene_long.csv (27 MB), module_trusted_term_gene_long.csv (12.9 MB), protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv (18 MB) or cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz to the browser.

Wire R3 back to R1 through consensus_presence.npz. A bitwise AND of one Pc column and one Uc column over the 18,068 gene ids gives, instantly, the exact gene list carrying both consensuses of a clicked edge - which is precisely the handoff from the network view to the per-gene UTR/protein sequence view. Precompute these gene lists for the 1,430 covered edges at build time so no numpy is needed in the browser.

Consider a build-time job to close the biggest gap: run motif_pair_network/17_consensus_association.py (or an equivalent using consensus_presence.npz) over the 757 cross-module cluster pairs so the M5-M1 and M1-M2 links - the ones the manuscript actually discusses - can show a consensus pair like every other edge. This is the single highest-value piece of new computation for R3.

Match the published figures exactly: modules M1..M6 in #4D4D4D, #0072B2, #E69F00, #009E73, #CC79A7, #56B4E9; regions protein #0072B2, utr5 #E69F00, utr3 #A85A00; short names M1-TF, M2-TF, M3-Secretory, M4-Immune, M5-RNA processing, M6-Translation. Because M1's gray is weak as a primary network color on a light background, either reserve gray for unassigned nodes and shift M1 to another Okabe-Ito hue, or keep gray and note the intentional deviation in theme.json.

gaps.gap: PWM/consensus coverage is partial: consensus_repertoire.pkl covers only the 513 clusters that are in a module, and only 451 of those have a significant STREME motif (1,226 consensus strings). 387 of the 900 clusters have no PWM, no consensus and no module.

For the missing logo, derive a display consensus at request time from the literal `motifs` strings of that cluster in the parquet (position-frequency of the aligned instances), and clearly badge the cluster as 'not in a module / no significant STREME consensus'.

gaps.gap: There is no precomputed 2-D layout for the module network that a JS renderer could consume. Fig 3e's node placement comes from a min-linear-arrangement inside 24_bipartite_pruned_ordered.py and Fig 3c's coordinates come from a v3-tree UMAP (sequence_analysis_v3_0515/07.umap_vis/.../cca_winner_umap.npy) that does not line up with v4 module definitions on its own.

gaps.workaround: Precompute coordinates in python once (reuse the module-ordering logic in 24_bipartite_pruned_ordered.py and node_select.py) and ship x/y per node in the JSON, exactly as 03.build_annotated_plotly_graph.py already does with its VERTICAL_GAP/HORIZONTAL_GAP deterministic bipartite layout.

gaps.gap: The two candidate 'gene carries motif' sources disagree by construction and no reconciliation table exists: identified_motifs_with_clusters (889,215 positional instances, 18,093 transcripts) vs consensus_presence.npz (fuzzy PWM carriers, 18,068 genes).
gaps.impact: Clicking an R3 edge and then jumping to one of its genes in the R1 view can show a gene with no visible highlighted instance of the motif that put it on that edge (the tier-B case, 53 of 106 in the M4 audit).

gaps.gap: No annotation exists that establishes physical protein-RNA interaction; RBP labels are gene-level co-occurrence in the same region, not binding under the motif.

findings.claim: Motif coordinates are 0-BASED, FULLY INCLUSIVE (closed interval). The exact and only correct slicing rule is seq[motif_start : motif_end + 1]. This reproduces the stored `motifs` string for 889,215 / 889,215 rows = 100.000000%, with zero exceptions, in all three regions.
findings.evidence: Ran /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/r1/s05_full.py (exhaustive, not sampled). Per region: utr5 118,997/118,997 (100.000000%); utr3 515,752/515,752 (100.000000%); protein 254,466/254,466 (100.000000%). Candidate conventions tested on 4,000 rows/region (s04_coords.py): seq[start:end] (0-based half-open) 0.0000% in all 3 regions; seq[start-1:end] (1-based inclusive) 0.15% utr5 / 0.63% utr3 / 0.00% protein (coincidental only); seq[start-1:end-1] 0.0000%; seq[start+1:end+1] 0.0000%. Corroborating identity over all 889,215 rows: (motif_end - motif_start + 1) == len(motifs) is True for 1.0 of rows, while (motif_end - motif_start) == len(motifs) is True for 0.0.
findings.portal_relevance: This is the single rule the whole R1 sequence viewer rests on. Highlight span = [motif_start, motif_end] inclusive; in JS use seq.slice(m.s, m.e + 1) and span length = m.e - m.s + 1. An off-by-one here silently shifts every highlight by one base.

findings.claim: No motif interval ever overruns its sequence: motif_end >= len(sequence) occurs 0 times in 889,215 rows, and max((end+1)/len(seq)) = 1.0000 exactly in each region.
findings.evidence: s05_full.py computed `over = (en >= slen).sum()` per region -> utr5 0, utr3 0, protein 0.
findings.portal_relevance: The viewer needs no clamping or bounds-guard logic; every interval is guaranteed in-range against the joined sequence.

findings.claim: The join key is `refseq_id_without_ver` in table C, and it is byte-identical to `best_refseq_mrna_id` (equality holds for all 21,667 rows). It gives 100% coverage: all 18,093 distinct sequence_ids in the motif table find a sequence row.
findings.evidence: s02_join.py / s03_dups.py. (c.refseq_id_without_ver == c.best_refseq_mrna_id).all() -> True. Match rates against the 18,093 motif sequence_ids: refseq_id_without_ver 18,093/18,093 (100.00%); best_refseq_mrna_id 18,093/18,093 (100.00%); `RefSeq mRNA ID` only 16,476/18,093 (91.06%); transcript_stable_id / `Transcript stable ID` / `Gene stable ID` 0/18,093 (0.00%).
findings.portal_relevance: Use refseq_id_without_ver. Do NOT use the `RefSeq mRNA ID` column - it would silently drop 1,617 genes (8.94%) from the portal.

findings.claim: Table C has 21,667 rows but only 19,210 distinct RefSeq ids. All 1,296 duplicated-refseq groups carry byte-identical sequence content, so deduplicating with drop_duplicates('refseq_id_without_ver') is lossless.
findings.evidence: s03_dups.py: 3,753 rows involved in duplicates across 1,296 distinct refseq ids; grouping each and comparing the concatenated utr5|cds|utr3|protein strings gave 1,296 groups with IDENTICAL content and 0 groups with differing content. Duplication arises because C is one-row-per-Ensembl-gene ('Gene stable ID' is unique across all 21,667 rows) and several ENSGs map to one RefSeq.
findings.portal_relevance: The shard builder can dedup on refseq without ambiguity or any need to pick a 'best' row. Keep the dropped ENSG/ENST values as a list per transcript to power Ensembl-ID search.

findings.claim: Motifs NEVER overlap within a (sequence_id, region). Maximum stacking depth is exactly 1 across all 53,367 (transcript, region) groups. A single-lane linear track is sufficient - no multi-track layout is needed.
findings.evidence: s07_overlap.py ran a sweep-line over every (sequence_id, region) group: max_depth describe() gives min=1, 50%=1, 90%=1, 95%=1, 99%=1, max=1 for all three regions (protein n=18,076; utr3 n=18,006; utr5 n=17,285). Overall value_counts of max_depth = {1: 53367} - a single bucket. Fraction needing >1 lane = 0.0. Independently confirmed in s08_disjoint.py: of 835,848 adjacent within-group pairs, overlapping pairs (gap<0) = 0. Also 0 exact duplicate (sequence_id, region, start, end) intervals in 889,215 rows.
findings.portal_relevance: Removes the hardest R1 rendering problem. The viewer can be a flat run-length-encoded span list over the sequence string - no interval-packing, no lane assignment, no z-ordering. Massively simplifies both layout and hit-testing for click/hover.

findings.claim: 6.0% of adjacent motif pairs ABUT exactly (gap == 0), and 9,838 of those abutting pairs share the same motif_cluster, so they would render as one indistinguishable block unless the viewer draws a separator.
findings.evidence: s08_disjoint.py / s15_cover.py: abutting pairs (gap==0) = 53,729 of 835,848 adjacent pairs (6.0%); of those, same-cluster = 9,838. Gap distribution: min 0, 25% 3, median 12, 75% 35, 99% 297, max 2,003.
findings.portal_relevance: Concrete rendering requirement: give each motif span its own element with a border/outline or 1px gap rather than merging contiguous same-color runs, otherwise 9,838 real pairs visually fuse into single false motifs.

findings.claim: UTR sequences and UTR motifs are stored in DNA alphabet (A/C/G/T - no U anywhere), but the manuscript writes all RNA motifs in RNA alphabet (UCAUC, UCUCC, GCCACC Kozak). The portal must transliterate T->U for display or it will not match the paper.
findings.evidence: s06_alpha.py: utr5 motif alphabet = ['A','C','G','T']; utr3 motif alphabet = ['A','C','G','T']; utr5_sequence and utr3_sequence alphabets = ['A','C','G','T']. s16_example.py: the manuscript's utr5_0096 'UCAUC' is stored as TCATC (3,442 UTR motif strings contain it); 'UCUCC' stored as TCTCC (14,696); Kozak 'GCCACC' (4,174); 'AGCAGA' (2,043). Protein alphabet is the 20 aa plus 'U' (selenocysteine).
findings.portal_relevance: Display-layer T->U map for utr5/utr3 tracks only (never for protein, where U means selenocysteine). Search must also accept U-form queries and normalize to T before matching stored strings.

findings.claim: Protein motif coordinates are in AMINO-ACID units indexed against protein_sequence, not nucleotide/CDS units.
findings.evidence: s05_full.py: protein_sequence[start:end+1] == motifs for 254,466/254,466 (100.000000%) protein rows, and the motif strings use the amino-acid alphabet (top chars L 283,239; S 232,876; G 202,831; A 191,973; P 190,415; R 189,929). Median cds_len/protein_len = 3.0047, confirming cds is the 3x nucleotide version and is NOT the coordinate frame.
findings.portal_relevance: The protein track indexes protein_sequence directly. Do not attempt CDS-space conversion. If a future nucleotide-space view is wanted, aa position i maps to cds[3i:3i+3].

findings.claim: gene_symbol -> sequence_id is effectively 1:1 and completely clean: 17,847 distinct symbols over 18,093 transcripts, with ZERO sequence_ids mapping to more than one symbol and zero null/empty symbols.
findings.evidence: s09_scale.py: 18,093 distinct (gene_symbol, sequence_id) pairs; gene_symbol nunique 17,847; sequence_id nunique 18,093; null=0, empty=0; sequence_ids mapping to >1 gene_symbol = 0. Genes with >1 transcript: 215 of 17,847 (1.20%), distribution {1:17632, 2:193, 3:17, 4:3, 5:1, 7:1}, max 7 (BAG6; then DDR1 5; HLA-DRB1, RPS9, VPS52 4).
findings.portal_relevance: A flat symbol->transcript index works for 98.8% of genes; only 215 genes need a transcript-picker UI. gene_symbol exists ONLY in table B (table C has no symbol column), so B is the authoritative source for search labels.

findings.claim: ENSG and ENST search are fully supported and unambiguous in the search direction: 20,481 ENSGs and 20,481 ENSTs are reachable for the 18,093 motif-bearing transcripts, and every ENSG maps to exactly one RefSeq.
findings.evidence: s10_ensembl.py: distinct ENSG reachable 20,481; distinct ENST reachable 20,481; ENSG -> n refseq max = 1, all==1 True. The reverse is many-to-one (refseq -> n ENSG mean 1.132, ==1 for 16,839, >1 for 1,254, max 42). Example: NM_000076 (CDKN1C) maps to ENSG00000129757 and ENSG00000273707. Versioned ids also available in 'Gene stable ID version' / 'Transcript stable ID version' (e.g. ENSG00000000003.17).
findings.portal_relevance: Build ENSG->refseq and ENST->refseq dicts (20,481 entries each); a user pasting either ID resolves to exactly one gene page with no disambiguation UI.

findings.claim: Static pre-sharded JSON is 158x faster than pyarrow filtering and 1,210x faster than cold pandas, with zero backend RAM. Measured per-gene query latency: static shard 1.13 ms, pyarrow filtered scan 179 ms, cold pandas full load 1,368 ms, warm indexed pandas 9.74 ms (but costs 782 MB resident).
findings.evidence: s21_bench.py over 18 real genes. (a) pandas read_parquet per query: mean 1,368 ms. (a2) loaded once + set_index('gene_symbol').sort_index(): mean 9.74 ms, max 127.73 ms, DataFrame memory_usage(deep=True) = 782 MB. (b) pyarrow.dataset to_table with pc.field('gene_symbol')==g: mean 179 ms, max 299 ms (13-col projection); with all 24 cols mean 150-265 ms. (c) gzipped shard read+parse: mean 1.131 ms, max 3.166 ms, mean wire size 3,741 B. duckdb is NOT installed (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'duckdb') so pyarrow was timed instead per instructions.
findings.portal_relevance: Decisive: the portal can and should be a STATIC site. No backend, no server RAM, no query layer. A CDN/GitHub-Pages/S3 deployment serves a gene page in one ~3.7 KB HTTP GET.

findings.claim: A key reason pyarrow filtering is slow: both motif parquets are written as a SINGLE row group, so predicate pushdown cannot prune anything and every query scans the full column.
findings.evidence: s01_schema.py: table A num_row_groups=1 (889,215 rows), table B num_row_groups=1 (889,215 rows), table C num_row_groups=1 (21,667 rows). s11_timing.py printed 'parquet row_groups=1 (no row-group pruning possible)'.
findings.portal_relevance: If a parquet-backed backend were ever chosen instead of static shards, the files would first have to be rewritten sorted by gene_symbol with small row groups. Another argument for the static-shard route.

findings.claim: A COMPLETE precomputed static shard set for all 18,093 transcripts (sequences + all motifs + all annotations) is 61.3 MB gzipped / 283.1 MB raw. This was built in full and measured, not extrapolated.
findings.evidence: s13_fullbuild.py built all 18,093 shards in 18 s. TOTAL raw 283.1 MB; TOTAL gzip 61.3 MB at compresslevel=6; compression ratio 4.62x. Per-shard gzip: mean 3,387 B, p50 3,046, p90 5,840, p99 8,263, max 10,739 B. On-disk `du -sh` = 93 MB (4 KB block padding inflates small files). A separate 300-shard sample extrapolated to 57.8 MB, and the 20-shard sample to 52.9 MB, both consistent with the exact 61.3 MB.
findings.portal_relevance: 61 MB total is trivially deployable to any static host and well under GitHub's 1 GB repo soft limit. The largest single gene page is 10.7 KB gzipped, so even the worst case loads instantly.

findings.claim: Annotations dominate shard size at 52.4% of payload, versus 32.5% for motif coordinates and only 15.1% for the sequences themselves.
findings.evidence: s14_composition.py over 400 random shards: seq mean 2,377 B (15.1%), motifs-without-annotations mean 5,135 B (32.5%), annotations mean 8,272 B (52.4%), total mean 15,784 B raw. Extrapolated raw over 18,093: seq 43.0 MB, motif coords 92.9 MB, annotations 149.7 MB.
findings.portal_relevance: If page weight ever matters, splitting annotations into a lazily-fetched second file per gene halves the initial payload to ~1.6 KB gzipped. At 3.4 KB mean this is not currently necessary - build it as one file.

findings.claim: The complete search index (17,847 symbols + 18,093 RefSeq + 20,481 ENSG + 20,481 ENST) is only 0.42 MB gzipped, small enough to load entirely client-side for instant offline autocomplete.
findings.evidence: s14_composition.py: full index raw 1.71 MB, gzip 0.42 MB. Symbol->transcript only: raw 0.43 MB, gzip 0.122 MB.
findings.portal_relevance: Ship the index as one file loaded at app boot. Typeahead then runs with zero network round-trips, which is what makes a static portal feel like a real search app.

findings.claim: Per-transcript scale is small and bounded - the viewer never has to render more than 189 motifs. Motifs per transcript (all regions): median 43, p99 138, max 189.
findings.evidence: s09_scale.py. Per (transcript, region) from s07_overlap.py: utr3 median 21, p90 65, p99 111, max 182; protein median 11, p90 28, p99 54, max 90; utr5 median 5, p90 15, p99 31, max 92.
findings.portal_relevance: Plain DOM spans are viable - no canvas/WebGL or virtualization needed. Worst case is ~189 elements per page.

findings.claim: Sequence lengths for motif-bearing transcripts are modest: utr5 median 186 / p99 1,447 / max 4,705 nt; utr3 median 1,062 / p99 6,008 / max 7,601 nt; protein median 401 / p99 2,142 / max 3,695 aa.
findings.evidence: s09_scale.py over the 18,093 motif-bearing transcripts. Total characters for utr5+utr3+protein across all of them = 42,060,999 (~42 MB raw).
findings.portal_relevance: Even the longest 3'UTR (7,601 nt) renders fine as wrapped monospace text at ~60 chars/line (~127 lines). No virtual scrolling required.

findings.claim: Motifs cover roughly a quarter to a third of every region's bases - dense enough that highlighting is the dominant visual, but not saturated.
findings.evidence: s15_cover.py, covered fraction per transcript: utr5 median 0.307 (p10 0.188, p90 0.464, max 0.761); utr3 median 0.261 (p10 0.197, p90 0.374, max 0.714); protein median 0.288 (p10 0.212, p90 0.366, max 0.674). No transcript exceeds 1.0, consistent with the zero-overlap finding.
findings.portal_relevance: Since ~30% of characters are highlighted, use subtle background fills with strong borders rather than saturated colors, or the page becomes unreadable. Color must encode cluster/module, not mere presence.

findings.claim: motif_cluster prefix matches region with perfect consistency, and cluster counts are exactly 300 protein + 500 utr3 + 100 utr5 = 900.
findings.evidence: s15_cover.py crosstab(region, cluster_prefix) is perfectly diagonal: protein/prot 254,466 with 0 off-diagonal; utr3/utr3 515,752; utr5/utr5 118,997. nunique per region: protein 300, utr3 500, utr5 100; total 900.
findings.portal_relevance: Region is derivable from the cluster id prefix, so shards need not repeat it. Also confirms the manuscript's 900-cluster figure against the raw data.

findings.claim: `unique_motif_id` identifies a motif STRING, not an instance: 577,186 ids over 889,215 rows, and 100% of id-groups contain exactly one distinct motif string. But 5.9% of these strings are assigned to MORE THAN ONE cluster depending on context.
findings.evidence: s08_disjoint.py: 577,186 groups; groups sharing one motif string = 1.0 (100%); groups sharing one motif_cluster = 0.9409 (so 5.91% span multiple clusters); 39,603 ids span >1 sequence_id, max 1,921 transcripts sharing one id. Example prot0000001 = 'AAAAA' appearing in 12 transcripts across clusters prot_0050, prot_0039, prot_0068, prot_0239, prot_0190, prot_0223.
findings.portal_relevance: Critical for R2. A 'motif page' keyed on unique_motif_id cannot show a single cluster - 5.91% of motif strings belong to several. The cluster assignment is per-INSTANCE and must be read from the row, never inferred from the string.

findings.claim: motif_cluster is a region-scoped relabelling of kmeans_label: each cluster maps to exactly one kmeans_label (max 1), while a kmeans_label can appear in up to 3 clusters because labels are reused across the three regions.
findings.evidence: s16_example.py: kmeans labels 500; n clusters per kmeans_label max 3, all==1 False; kmeans labels per motif_cluster max 1, mean 1.00. Per-region kmeans nunique: protein 300, utr3 500, utr5 100.
findings.portal_relevance: Explains the manuscript's '900 clusters from 500 kmeans labels'. Always key cluster logic on motif_cluster (globally unique), never on kmeans_label (ambiguous across regions).

findings.claim: DATA-QUALITY BUG the portal must guard against: the `MobIDB annotation` column - a protein-disorder database - is populated on 67.0% of utr5 rows and 25.3% of utr3 rows with protein disorder terms, using the identical 87-value vocabulary as the protein rows. `idpo_annotations` and `signalp_annotation` leak the same way.
findings.evidence: s17_anncheck.py non-empty fraction by region: MobIDB annotation utr5 0.6698 / utr3 0.2525 / protein 0.8721; idpo_annotations utr5 0.0060 / utr3 0.0022 / protein 0.0075; signalp_annotation utr5 0.0031 / utr3 0.0006 / protein 0.0012. UTR-row MobiDB values are protein terms such as 'homology-domain-merge' (111,391), 'prediction-plddt-alphafold' (109,697), 'prediction-disorder-alphafold' (73,068). set(utr vocab) == set(protein vocab) is True, 87 values each. The authors' own annotation_coverage_stats.json declares mobidb applies='protein' with denominator 254,466, i.e. UTR values were never meant to be counted.
findings.portal_relevance: Rendering these verbatim would tell a user that a 3'UTR nucleotide motif has 'intrinsic protein disorder' - a scientifically embarrassing, visibly wrong claim. The shard builder MUST drop protein-layer annotation columns on utr5/utr3 rows and RNA-layer columns on protein rows.

findings.claim: The correct annotation filter rule is the `applies` field in the authors' own annotation_coverage_stats.json, and applying it reproduces all 8 published coverage numbers EXACTLY.
findings.evidence: s18_verify_filter.py recomputed each database's annotated-row count under its declared `applies` mask and matched the published value for all 8: rbp (applies=utr) 325,996 = 325,996 (51.358%); mirna (utr3) 24,228 (4.698%); interpro (protein) 172,421 (67.758%); elm 797 (0.313%); uniprot 229,532 (90.201%); mobidb 221,909 (87.206%); idpo 1,908 (0.750%); signalp 298 (0.117%). All 8 report YES.
findings.portal_relevance: annotation_coverage_stats.json is directly reusable as the portal's annotation-rendering config: it carries `display` (human label), `source` (database name), `layer` (RNA/protein) and `applies` (region filter) per database. Drive the annotation UI from this file rather than hardcoding.

findings.claim: Searching a well-known long gene such as TTN returns NOTHING: 1,117 of the 19,210 RefSeq transcripts have no motifs, and there is a hard transcript-length cutoff at 7,784 nt (the model's context limit).
findings.evidence: s22_missing.py: max transcript_length WITH motifs = 7,784; 666 transcripts exceed that and ALL 666 lack motifs (verified (~over.has).all() is True); a further 451 are under the cap but still lack motifs. Missing-transcript lengths: median 8,260, p99 23,841, max 37,239. The largest is NM_001267550 / ENSG00000155657 = TTN. Motif-bearing lengths: median 1,940, p99 6,809.
findings.portal_relevance: The search index must be built from the motif table's 17,847 symbols only, and the UI needs an explicit 'not covered - transcript exceeds the 7,784 nt model context' empty state. Silently returning no results for TTN would read as a broken portal.

findings.claim: Not every transcript has all three tracks: 808 transcripts have no 5'UTR motifs, 87 no 3'UTR motifs, 17 no protein motifs; only 17,191 of 18,093 (95.0%) have all three.
findings.evidence: s15_cover.py: utr5 have 17,285 / MISSING 808; utr3 have 18,006 / MISSING 87; protein have 18,076 / MISSING 17; all-three intersection 17,191.
findings.portal_relevance: The three-track viewer must render an empty-but-present track (sequence shown, no highlights) rather than hiding the panel, for 902 genes.

findings.claim: End-to-end validation on ACTB (NM_001101) confirms the whole R1 pipeline including annotations, and independently corroborates the science: all 3 of its 5'UTR motifs fall in cluster utr5_0004, the Kozak/translation cluster the manuscript assigns to module M6.
findings.evidence: s16_example.py: ACTB utr5 len 84, utr3 len 600, protein len 375; 3 utr5 + 13 utr3 + 4 protein motifs, every slice assertion passed. utr5 [5,15] 'CGAGACCGCGT' cluster utr5_0004 with RBPs_eCLIP ['GEMIN5','PUM1','SERBP1']; utr3 [82,126] a 45-nt AU-rich 'TATTTGTTTT...' in utr3_0313 with RBPs_eCLIP ['DDX55','NKRF','SUB1','TIAL1'] (TIAL1 is a canonical ARE-binding protein); protein [23,27] 'DDAPR' cluster prot_0040 with interpro 'ATPase, nucleotide binding domain,Actin family'.
findings.portal_relevance: A ready-made smoke-test case for the build: ACTB should show 3/13/4 motifs, utr5 all in utr5_0004, and TIAL1 on the AU-rich 3'UTR element. Also a good default landing-page example.

findings.claim: `cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz` covers ALL 900 clusters with 260,572 enrichment rows from 10 annotation sources - far better than the 37-cluster cluster_term_labels.csv - and 463 clusters (51.4%) carry at least one FDR<0.05 term.
findings.evidence: s20_enrich.py: distinct clusters 900 (100.0% of 900); by region protein 300 / utr3 500 / utr5 100; sources InterPro 143,254, eCLIP 38,097, PAR-CLIP 23,270, MobiDB 16,028, miR 15,798, iCLIP-P 12,679, iCLIP-C 9,519, IDPO 1,187, ELM 694, SignalP 46; rows with fdr_cluster<0.05 = 25,750 spanning 463 clusters. Columns include cluster, region, source, term, k, n, K, N, fold, p, fdr_cluster, or_mh, fdr_global, display, informative.
findings.portal_relevance: This is the asset that makes R2 ('annotations on the motif cluster') work at full 900-cluster scale. cluster_term_labels.csv (37 clusters) and bipartite_nodes_all6.csv (52 nodes) are figure-only subsets and must not be used as the portal's backing data.

findings.claim: module_gene_index.csv carries a `refseq_ids` column that joins to sequence_id with 100% precision, letting every gene page show its module membership - but only 48.9% of portal genes have one.
findings.evidence: s19_assets.py / s20_enrich.py: module_gene_index.csv has 12,345 rows, 8,720 distinct gene_symbols across 6 modules, columns [module_id, gene_symbol, n_transcripts, refseq_ids, paralog_families, n_sig_terms_hit, n_trusted_terms_hit, trusted_terms]. All 8,720 symbols are present in the motif table's gene_symbol (100.0%). Its 8,846 distinct refseq ids all match a motif sequence_id (100.0%), covering 8,846 of 18,093 transcripts (48.9%).
findings.portal_relevance: Gene page can render a 'Modules' section for 8,846 transcripts. The other 9,247 need an explicit 'not assigned to a module' state - and that absence is scientifically meaningful (module membership required passing the phylogenetic-independence filter), so it should be explained, not hidden.

gaps.gap: consensus_meta.csv (the STREME consensus strings needed to label motif clusters in R2 and R3) covers only 451 of 900 clusters (50.1%).
gaps.impact: Half of all cluster detail pages, and any meta-module edge touching them, have no consensus string to display. A user clicking a node in the R3 view has a coin-flip chance of seeing no sequence logo or consensus label.
gaps.workaround: Three options in ascending cost: (1) derive a cheap position-weight consensus directly from the member motif strings in table B for the 449 uncovered clusters - all instances are available, so an IUPAC or most-frequent-base consensus is computable in seconds; (2) rerun STREME using the existing pipeline in motif_pair_network/ (fasta/ inputs and streme_out_full/ already exist for 515 clusters, so the gap may be smaller than the CSV suggests - check streme_out_full/ before regenerating); (3) show the top-N most frequent member motif strings instead of a consensus, which is honest and needs no new computation.

gaps.gap: 449 of 900 clusters (48.6%) have no term passing FDR<0.05 in cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz, so they have no interpretable functional annotation at all.
gaps.impact: R2 requires 'annotations on the motif'. For nearly half of clusters the honest answer is 'no significant enrichment', which is a weak detail page.
gaps.workaround: Show the top terms by fold-enrichment with their FDR displayed even when non-significant, clearly greyed and labelled 'not significant'. Fall back to per-instance annotations from table B (RBPs_eCLIP, InterPro etc.), which cover 63.9% of individual motifs and are independent of cluster-level enrichment.

gaps.gap: 9,247 of 18,093 transcripts (51.1%) belong to no module, and 1,117 RefSeq transcripts (including TTN and other long genes) have no motifs at all and are absent from the portal entirely.
gaps.impact: Roughly half of gene pages cannot show the R3 module context, and a user searching a famous long gene gets an empty result that looks like a bug.
gaps.workaround: For the no-module case, state plainly that the gene's motif clusters did not pass the phylogenetic-independence filter (2,620 of 180,000 pairs passed) - this is a real scientific result, not missing data. For the no-motif case, precompute a small 'excluded transcripts' list with the reason ('transcript length 37,239 nt exceeds the 7,784 nt model context') so search can return an informative empty state.

gaps.gap: Table C has no gene_symbol column, so the 1,117 motif-free transcripts cannot be labelled with a gene name from the available data.
gaps.impact: The portal cannot tell a user searching 'TTN' that TTN exists but was excluded - it can only fail to find the symbol, which is indistinguishable from a typo.
gaps.workaround: Recover symbols for the excluded set from module_gene_index.csv's gene_symbol<->refseq_ids mapping where present, or add a small external RefSeq->symbol map (NCBI gene2refseq, or a one-off pyensembl/mygene lookup for just 1,117 ids). Cost is a single offline script; the result is a ~30 KB JSON.

gaps.gap: duckdb is not installed in the bio environment.
gaps.impact: Prevented the requested (b) duckdb timing comparison; pyarrow.dataset was timed instead as instructed.
gaps.workaround: None needed - the measured result makes the point moot. Static shards at 1.13 ms are 158x faster than the pyarrow alternative, so no query engine is required at all. If a backend is ever added, note both motif parquets are single-row-group and would need rewriting sorted by gene_symbol first.

gaps.gap: There is no per-nucleotide NTScore/SeqScore track in any of the three tables - only per-motif motif_score, motif_entropy and (protein-only) plddt.
gaps.impact: The manuscript's central quantity, the per-nucleotide conditional log-probability, cannot be plotted as a continuous track beneath the sequence, which would be the most compelling R1 visualization.
gaps.workaround: Use motif_score as a per-motif bar (it is present for 100% of rows) and plddt as a protein confidence track (protein rows only). If a true per-base NTScore track is wanted, it would have to be regenerated by rerunning MIRTO inference - out of scope for the portal build; confirm with the user whether such a cache exists elsewhere before promising the feature.

reusable_assets.what: Working shard builder that already produced the complete, verified 18,093-transcript static dataset (283.1 MB raw / 61.3 MB gzipped) in 18 seconds. Handles the region-keyed motif grouping, plddt-on-protein-only logic, null/NaN cleaning of the 6 list-columns and 5 string-columns, and gzip output.
reusable_assets.how_to_reuse: Adopt as the portal's data build step almost as-is. Two required edits before production: (1) drop protein-layer annotation columns on utr5/utr3 rows per the annotation_coverage_stats.json `applies` field, to fix the MobiDB leak; (2) add the ensg/enst id lists (currently stubbed as None). Point OUT at the portal's public/data directory.

reusable_assets.what: The complete built shard set: 18,093 files named <refseq>.json.gz, each containing {transcript, gene, seq:{utr5,utr3,protein}, motifs:{utr5:[],utr3:[],protein:[]}} with s/e/seq/c/u/sc/en/plddt/ann per motif. Mean 3,387 B gzipped, max 10,739 B.
reusable_assets.how_to_reuse: Usable immediately for prototyping the R1 viewer against real data without rerunning the build. Note it still contains the MobiDB leak, so regenerate from the corrected builder before shipping.

reusable_assets.what: Machine-readable annotation registry: per database a `display` label, `source` (POSTAR3/ENCODE eCLIP, TargetScan, InterPro, ELM, UniProt, MobiDB, IDPO, SignalP), `layer` (RNA/protein), `applies` (utr/utr3/protein), denominator, n_annotated and pct. Verified to reproduce all 8 coverage numbers exactly.
reusable_assets.how_to_reuse: Ship verbatim as the portal's annotation config. Drive both the region-filter rule that fixes the MobiDB leak and the UI's source labels/coverage badges from it, instead of hardcoding database names.

reusable_assets.what: 260,572 enrichment rows covering all 900 clusters across 10 annotation sources, with fold, p, or_mh, fdr_cluster, fdr_global, display and an `informative` flag. 463 clusters have >=1 term at FDR<0.05.
reusable_assets.how_to_reuse: The backing data for R2 cluster annotation pages. Pre-slice into 900 small per-cluster JSON files (filter fdr_cluster<0.05, keep top ~20 by fold) at build time; the whole set will be a few MB. Use this rather than cluster_term_labels.csv.

reusable_assets.what: 1,226 STREME consensus strings for 451 clusters: cid, cluster, module, region, consensus, coverage, carriers (e.g. prot_0001#0 LPSQPL coverage 0.390 carriers 189). Mean 2.72 consensus per cluster, max 10.
reusable_assets.how_to_reuse: Cluster headline labels for R2/R3 nodes. Covers only 50.1% of clusters - pair with a computed fallback consensus for the remaining 449 (see gaps).

reusable_assets.what: 12,345 rows mapping 8,720 gene symbols to the 6 modules, with a refseq_ids column that joins to sequence_id at 100% precision, plus n_transcripts, paralog_families, n_sig_terms_hit, n_trusted_terms_hit and trusted_terms.
reusable_assets.how_to_reuse: Gives every gene page its module cross-link (R1 -> R3 navigation) and every module page its gene list. Join on refseq_ids -> sequence_id; covers 8,846 of 18,093 transcripts.

reusable_assets.what: Existing per-gene motif sequence-view code and curated examples: examples_lib.py, build_examples.py, examples_table.csv/.md, alu_segment_01_seqview.py, h2az2/hba/dnajb4/mlxipl signature builders, build_m6_kozak.py.
reusable_assets.how_to_reuse: examples_lib.py and alu_segment_01_seqview.py already solve 'render a sequence with motif spans' in matplotlib - read them for the author's established color conventions and track ordering so the web viewer matches the manuscript figures. examples_table.csv is a ready-made curated list of showcase genes for the portal's landing page.

reusable_assets.what: Verification script that recomputes all 8 published annotation coverage percentages under the region-filter rule and confirms exact agreement.
reusable_assets.how_to_reuse: Keep as a build-time regression test: if the shard builder's annotation filtering ever drifts, this catches it by comparing against the authors' published numbers.

reusable_assets.what: Exhaustive coordinate validator proving seq[start:end+1]==motifs for all 889,215 rows in 0.5 s.
reusable_assets.how_to_reuse: Run as a build-time assertion before shard generation, so any future data refresh that changes the coordinate convention fails loudly instead of silently shifting every highlight.

recommendations: BUILD THE PORTAL AS A FULLY STATIC SITE - no backend. This is settled by measurement, not preference: a pre-sharded gene page loads in 1.13 ms versus 179 ms for pyarrow filtering and 1,368 ms for cold pandas, needs 0 MB of server RAM versus 782 MB for a warm pandas server, and the entire dataset is 61.3 MB gzipped. Deploy to GitHub Pages, S3+CloudFront or Netlify. This also removes the deployment-target unknown from the plan, since a static bundle runs anywhere including from the user's laptop via `python -m http.server`.

Use exactly this slicing rule everywhere and write it into a shared constant: highlight span = [motif_start, motif_end] INCLUSIVE, so in JS `seq.slice(m.s, m.e + 1)` and length `m.e - m.s + 1`. Verified at 100.000000% over all 889,215 rows. Add the s05_full.py assertion to the build so a future data refresh cannot silently shift every highlight by one base.

Render each region as a SINGLE-LANE track. The zero-overlap finding (max stacking depth exactly 1 across all 53,367 transcript-region groups) eliminates interval packing, lane assignment and z-ordering. Emit a flat run-length-encoded alternation of unhighlighted text and motif spans over the sequence string - the simplest possible implementation is also the correct one here.

Give every motif span its own bordered element rather than merging adjacent same-color runs. 53,729 adjacent pairs abut exactly (gap 0) and 9,838 of those share a cluster, so without a separator they fuse into single false motifs. A 1px gap or inset outline is sufficient.

Fix the annotation region leak in the shard builder before shipping. Filter every annotation column by the `applies` field in annotation_coverage_stats.json - protein-layer columns (MobiDB, IDPO, SignalP, InterPro, UniProt, ELM) must be dropped on utr5/utr3 rows, RNA-layer columns on protein rows. Unfiltered, the portal would tell users a 3'UTR nucleotide motif has 'intrinsic protein disorder' on 67% of 5'UTR motifs. The filter is verified to reproduce all 8 of the authors' published coverage numbers exactly.

Transliterate T to U for 5'UTR and 3'UTR display only, never for protein (where U is selenocysteine). Storage is DNA alphabet but the manuscript writes every RNA motif in RNA alphabet, so without this the portal will not match the paper's own motif names (UCAUC, UCUCC, GCCACC). Make sequence search accept both forms and normalize to T before matching.

Join on refseq_id_without_ver and deduplicate table C with drop_duplicates('refseq_id_without_ver') - verified lossless, since all 1,296 duplicate groups carry byte-identical sequences. Do not use the `RefSeq mRNA ID` column, which would silently drop 1,617 genes (8.94%).

Ship the full search index (17,847 symbols + 18,093 RefSeq + 20,481 ENSG + 20,481 ENST) as one 0.42 MB gzipped file loaded at app boot, giving instant client-side typeahead with no network round-trips. Support ENSG/ENST paste-in directly - each maps to exactly one RefSeq, so no disambiguation UI is needed. Only 215 genes (1.20%) have multiple transcripts and need a picker.

Design explicit, informative empty states rather than letting absences look like bugs - there are three distinct kinds. (1) 1,117 transcripts have no motifs at all, 666 of them because they exceed the hard 7,784 nt model-context cutoff, so searching TTN must say so rather than returning nothing. (2) 902 transcripts are missing at least one of the three tracks - show the sequence with no highlights, do not hide the panel. (3) 9,247 transcripts belong to no module, which is a real scientific result of the phylogenetic-independence filter and should be explained.

Key R2 cluster pages on motif_cluster (globally unique, 900 values, region derivable from the prefix), never on kmeans_label (ambiguous - reused across regions). Critically, read the cluster from the motif ROW, not from the motif string: unique_motif_id identifies a string, and 5.91% of strings are assigned to more than one cluster depending on context.

Use cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz (all 900 clusters, 260,572 rows) as the backing data for R2, pre-sliced at build time into 900 small per-cluster JSON files. Do not build on cluster_term_labels.csv (37 clusters) or bipartite_nodes_all6.csv (52 nodes) - these are figure-only subsets that would cover 4% of the space.

Keep shards as one file per gene rather than splitting annotations out. Annotations are 52.4% of payload and could be lazily loaded to halve the initial fetch, but at 3.4 KB mean and 10.7 KB worst case gzipped there is no need - the simpler single-fetch design is right until measurement says otherwise.

Use plain DOM spans with no canvas, WebGL or virtualization. Worst case is 189 motifs and a 7,601 nt sequence on one page; median is 43 motifs. Since ~30% of characters are highlighted, use subtle background fills with strong borders and reserve saturated color for encoding cluster or module identity, or the page becomes unreadable.

Use ACTB (NM_001101) as the build smoke test and default landing example: it should show exactly 3 5'UTR, 13 3'UTR and 4 protein motifs, with all three 5'UTR motifs in cluster utr5_0004 (the Kozak/translation cluster the manuscript assigns to module M6) and TIAL1, a canonical ARE-binding protein, annotated on its 45-nt AU-rich 3'UTR element. This validates coordinates, join, clustering and annotations in one glance.

Surface the statistical caveat structurally, not as fine print. Module membership is co-occurrence (NPMI with APC correction plus a phylogenetic-independence filter that passed only 2,620 of 180,000 pairs), not demonstrated physical interaction. Put that sentence on every module and edge detail view, and consider exposing the per-pair n_indep_clades and frac_co_ZNF from protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv so users can judge evidence strength themselves - the RAW_top30_annotated.csv `verdict` column already names specific ZNF clade artifacts and would make an honest 'known artifacts' page.

findings.claim: motif_cluster is EXACTLY the region-prefixed, zero-padded 4-digit kmeans_label: motif_cluster = f'{prefix}_{kmeans_label:04d}' with prefix in {prot, utr3, utr5}. Verified with 0 mismatches across all 889,215 rows.
findings.evidence: /opt/anaconda3/envs/bio/bin/python on identified_motifs_with_clusters.0513.parquet: `(motif_cluster.str.split('_').str[1].astype(int) == kmeans_label).all()` -> True; mismatch rows = 0. Crosstab(region, prefix) is perfectly block-diagonal: protein->prot 254,466; utr3->utr3 515,752; utr5->utr5 118,997.
findings.portal_relevance: The portal can derive cluster id <-> (region, kmeans label) with pure string ops, no lookup table. A cluster URL slug like /cluster/utr3_0215 is canonical and self-describing.

findings.claim: kmeans was run PER MODALITY, not once with k=500. Protein uses labels 0-299 (300 clusters), utr3 uses 0-499 (500), utr5 uses 0-99 (100). 300+500+100 = 900 motif_clusters. There is no single global 500-label space.
findings.evidence: df.groupby('region')['kmeans_label'].nunique() -> protein 300 (min 0 max 299), utr3 500 (min 0 max 499), utr5 100 (min 0 max 99). df.kmeans_label.nunique() == 500 only because utr3's range is the widest.
findings.portal_relevance: Never display a bare kmeans_label in the UI; the same integer (e.g. 96) means three different clusters. Always show the full motif_cluster id. Cluster pickers must be region-scoped.

findings.claim: unique_motif_id is a dedup key on (region, motif string), NOT a per-instance id: 577,186 unique_motif_ids over 889,215 instances, and exactly 577,186 distinct (region, motifs) pairs. 563,143 distinct motif strings globally (the 14,043 difference = strings occurring in more than one region). 537,493 uids occur exactly once; max 2,242 instances for one uid.
findings.evidence: df.unique_motif_id.nunique()=577186; len(df[['region','motifs']].drop_duplicates())=577186; df.motifs.nunique()=563143; groupby(uid).motifs.nunique().max()==1; instance-count value_counts {1:537493, 2:19114, 3:6019, 4:3192, 5:2041, 6:1327}, max 2242 (uid utr30108178, motif 'CTGGA').
findings.portal_relevance: The hierarchy is instance (raw_motif_index) -> unique_motif_id (region+string) -> motif_cluster. A motif detail page keyed on unique_motif_id shows every transcript carrying that exact string in that region.

findings.claim: CRITICAL: the same unique_motif_id can be assigned to MANY different clusters. 34,110 uids (5.91% of all uids; 85.9% of the 39,693 multi-instance uids) appear in >=2 clusters; median 2, p90 10, p99 50, max 176. The extreme case is utr30108178 = 'CTGGA', 1,101 instances spread over 176 distinct utr3 clusters.
findings.evidence: groupby('unique_motif_id').motif_cluster.nunique(): (>1).sum()=34110 of 577186; among the 39,693 uids with >1 instance, 34,110 (85.9%) span >=2 clusters; describe -> mean 5.18, p90 10, p99 50, max 176.
findings.portal_relevance: Clustering is on CONTEXTUAL motif embeddings, not on the literal substring. The portal must NOT present a cluster as 'the set of strings X, Y, Z' or imply that seeing CTGGA tells you the cluster. On the transcript view (R1), a highlighted motif instance must carry its own row-level motif_cluster, not one looked up from the string.

findings.claim: There are NO tiny clusters. Minimum cluster size is 218 instances (utr3_0359); 0 clusters have <100 instances. Overall: instances min 218 / p10 603 / median 920 / p90 1,405 / max 5,755 (utr3_0188). Distinct genes min 23 (prot_0092) / median 565 / p90 902 / max 4,532 (utr3_0071). Distinct transcripts min 24 / median 569 / max 4,571.

Every one of the 900 cluster pages will have enough members for stable statistics, gene lists and histograms. Cluster gene lists are large (median 565) so the UI needs paging/virtualisation, not a plain list.

findings.claim: Motif instance lengths inside a cluster are highly HETEROGENEOUS, so a naive stacked-string sequence logo is not viable. The median cluster has 37 (utr3) / 45.5 (prot) / 45 (utr5) distinct member lengths, and only 21-25% of members share the modal length. Only 32 of 900 clusters have >=50% of members at the modal length; 214 reach >=30%.

Concrete: utr3_0215 n=566, modal_len=5, only 184 at modal, 30 distinct lengths. Overall motif_length by region: protein mean 11.0 (5-535), utr3 mean 14.5 (5-55), utr5 mean 13.5 (5-55).
findings.portal_relevance: The logo MUST come from a STREME PWM, not from aligning member strings. Any plan that says 'stack the motif strings and draw a logo' will produce garbage for 868 of 900 clusters.

findings.claim: Real letter-probability matrices (PWMs) exist on disk in MEME/STREME format and parse cleanly to JSON. streme.txt layout: 'ALPHABET= <letters>', a background-frequency block, then per motif 'MOTIF <n>-<CONSENSUS> STREME-<n>' followed by 'letter-probability matrix: alength= A w= W nsites= N E= <float>' and W rows of A floats each summing to 1.0000. alength=20 (ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY) for protein, alength=4 (ACGU, U not T) for UTR.
findings.evidence: Parsed with a regex in /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/a4_streme.py. prot_0000: 20 motifs, motif0 '1-LPALQY' w=6 nsites=8 E=1.1, pwm 6x20, row sum 1.0000, JSON 30,466 bytes. utr3_0215: 12 motifs, motif0 '1-YCUCC' w=5 nsites=394 E=9.2e-14, pwm 5x4, JSON 4,120 bytes. utr5_0096: 12 motifs, motif0 '1-AGSAGA' w=6 nsites=74 E=1.3e-4.
findings.portal_relevance: A JS logo renderer (logojs / d3 / hand-rolled SVG) can be fed directly. Note the RNA alphabet is ACGU while the raw motifs column in the parquet uses T (utr30108178 = 'CTGGA') - the portal must T->U convert when overlaying a consensus on a sequence, or U->T the other way.

findings.claim: STREME PWM coverage is 466 of 900 clusters (utr3 249, prot 151, utr5 66); 434 clusters have NO PWM anywhere. The three output dirs cover exactly 513 clusters, which are exactly the modules.json members; 387 clusters were never run. Of the 513 run, 62 protein clusters produced 0 significant motifs (test_pvalue<0.05), leaving 451 with a significant repertoire; 15 of those 62 still have a 2-motif PWM in the older streme_out/ cache.

Union of in-memory PWM sources (repertoire n_sig>0, streme_pos_cache_all6, streme_topN_cache) = 466.
findings.portal_relevance: Without new computation, 434 of 900 cluster pages have no sequence logo. Cross-tab: 258 clusters have BOTH a PWM and an auto-name, 229 have NEITHER.

findings.claim: The gap is fixable: the STREME binary is installed and runnable, and a fresh run costs ~64 s for a protein cluster and ~5-10 s for a UTR cluster. Filling all 387 missing clusters is ~2.4 CPU-hours single-threaded, ~15 min at the pipeline's 10 workers.

findings.claim: protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv is a COMPLETE dense grid of 300 protein clusters x 600 UTR clusters = 180,000 rows, and the UTR side includes BOTH utr3 (150,000 rows, 500 clusters) and utr5 (30,000 rows, 100 clusters). 2,620 rows pass the phylogenetic-independence filter.

findings.portal_relevance: For ANY of the 900 clusters the portal can show a complete partner ranking - protein clusters get 600 candidate partners, UTR clusters get 300 - with no missing cells. The 0.74 MB filtered edge file (phylo-pass OR npmi>0.1, 7,210 rows) is small enough to ship statically.

findings.claim: The phylo filter is effectively a superset-subset of an NPMI threshold: EVERY one of the 2,620 passing pairs has npmi_mip_APC > 0.1 (min 0.1001), n_indep_clades >= 8 (median 13), co_count >= 10 (median 49), and frac_co_ZNF <= 0.40 (0 pairs above 0.5). Full npmi_mip_APC distribution: min -0.8397, p50 -0.0369, p90 0.0587, p95 0.0895, p99 0.1826, p99.9 0.4023, max 0.8752.
findings.evidence: d[d.passes_phylo_filter].npmi_mip_APC.min()=0.1001; (>0.1).all()==True; n_indep_clades min 8 median 13; co_count min 10 median 49; frac_co_ZNF max 0.400. Threshold counts on the full grid: npmi>0 -> 58,204; >0.02 -> 41,417; >0.05 -> 21,873; >0.1 -> 7,210; >0.15 -> 2,995; >0.2 -> 1,414.
findings.portal_relevance: Gives the UI two principled tiers with no arbitrary numbers: STRICT = passes_phylo_filter (2,620 edges, matches the manuscript) and RELAXED = npmi_mip_APC>0.1 (7,210 edges, the exact superset). Do NOT default to npmi>0.05 - it lights up all 600 UTR clusters with a median of 33 partners each.

findings.claim: Partner counts per cluster are UI-friendly at the strict threshold but coverage is incomplete. passes_phylo_filter: 318 of 600 UTR clusters have >=1 partner (min 1, median 5, p90 23, max 39) and 201 of 300 protein clusters (median 8, p90 35, max 62). Relaxing to npmi>0.1 reaches 537/600 UTR (median 8, max 58) and 298/300 protein. npmi>0.15 alone gives 344/600 UTR (median 5, max 41).
findings.evidence: groupby('utr').size() and groupby('protein').size() on each filtered slice (scratchpad/b1_pairs.py). Concrete: utr3_0215 has 300 candidate protein partners of which exactly 2 pass phylo; utr5_0090 has 39 passing; utr5_0004 has 15; utr5_0096 has 5; utr5_0079 has 8; utr3_0463 has 6.
findings.portal_relevance: The partner table is always short enough to render in full (max 62 rows). But 282 of 600 UTR clusters have ZERO passing partner - those pages need an explicit 'no phylogenetically independent protein partner' state plus a one-click relaxed view, not an empty table.

findings.claim: The R2 chain 'UTR motif cluster -> partner protein clusters -> protein features' resolves end-to-end for essentially every passing edge: 2,614 of 2,620 (99.8%) passing edges have a protein partner carrying >=1 FDR<0.05 enriched term, and 317 of the 318 UTR clusters with a passing partner can therefore show real protein features. The reverse direction is much weaker: only 1,180 of 2,620 (45.0%) passing edges have a UTR side with any FDR<0.05 RBP/miRNA term.
findings.evidence: Join protein_utr_FINAL_scores (passes_phylo_filter) to the top-3 FDR<0.05 terms per cluster from cluster_term_enrichment. Verified worked examples: utr3_0215 -> prot_0038 npmi_APC 0.292, phylo_score 0.428, co_count 21, 8 clades, ZNF 0.0, features 'Immunoglobulin-like domain superfamily (InterPro, 25.4x)'. utr5_0004 -> prot_0040 npmi_APC 0.628, score 1.769, co 175, 23 clades, 'Histone-fold (InterPro, 26.5x)' (the M6 edge). utr5_0079 -> prot_0072 npmi_APC 0.251, score 0.517, 'RNA-binding domain superfamily (InterPro, 11.1x); phase separation (curated) (MobiDB, 9.3x)' (the M5 edge). utr5_0096 -> prot_0038/prot_0241/prot_0060/prot_0272/prot_0225 (the M4 immune edges).
findings.portal_relevance: R2's headline requirement is satisfiable with existing files and a two-table join - no new statistics needed. The asymmetry means the UTR cluster page should lead with the PROTEIN partner's features (well covered) and treat its own RBP annotation as supporting evidence.

findings.claim: plddt exists only for protein motifs: 254,466 non-null values, 0 for utr3/utr5. Per-cluster medians span 0.215 to 0.972 (mean 0.730, median 0.801, p10 0.376) - a genuinely discriminating axis separating ordered-domain clusters from IDR clusters. motif_score is negative log-prob-like (min -4.83, median -1.135, max ~0); cluster medians differ sharply by region (prot median -1.49 with spread -2.90 to -0.01; utr3 -1.12; utr5 -1.09). motif_entropy median 1.179 overall (prot cluster medians span 0.04-2.85, utr3 0.31-1.33).
findings.evidence: df.plddt.notna().sum()=254466, all region=='protein'. groupby(cluster) medians describe as quoted. motif_score describe: mean -1.2114, std 0.6371, min -4.83125, q25 -1.4376, q50 -1.1352, q75 -0.8581, max -3.9e-06. motif_entropy: mean 1.2176, std 0.5599, min 5.6e-05, max 2.9469.
findings.portal_relevance: Protein cluster pages get a real structural axis (pLDDT distribution) that UTR pages cannot have; the layout must branch on region rather than showing an empty pLDDT panel for 600 of 900 clusters.

findings.claim: Module assignment exists for only 513 of 900 clusters (utr3 249, protein 198, utr5 66) - and the six modules.json entries hold far more members than the 52 figure nodes: M1 39 protein + 67 UTR (774 edges, mean_score 0.3633), M2 39+73 (409, 0.3182), M3 62+71 (385, 0.3119), M4 20+53 (123, 0.3510), M5 24+33 (126, 0.3196), M6 14+18 (43, 0.3827). Their union is exactly the 513 clusters, identical to consensus_scope_clusters.csv (0 symmetric difference). 387 clusters have no module.
findings.evidence: json.load(modules.json) -> list of 6 dicts with keys [protein_motifs, utr_motifs, n_protein, n_utr, n_edges, mean_score, mean_indep_clades, mean_frac_ZNF, top_pairs, module_id]; len(protein_motifs) matches n_protein for all six; union 513, Counter {utr3 249, prot 198, utr5 66}. top_pairs holds 5 strings each formatted '<prot>x<utr>' e.g. 'prot_0135xutr3_0020'. bipartite_nodes_all6.csv has only 52 rows (the <=5-per-module-per-side display cap).

findings.claim: RAW_top30_annotated.csv contains a human-written verdict column that is ready-made copy for the mandatory statistical-artifact caveat: of the top 30 RAW-NPMI pairs, 25 are labelled 'ZNF clade artifact', 4 'single-clade / weak', and only 1 'survives'.
findings.evidence: pd.read_csv shape (30,16), verdict.value_counts() = {'ZNF clade artifact':25, 'single-clade / weak':4, 'survives':1}. Row 1: prot_0228 x utr5_0020, co_count 289, npmi_raw 0.8969, npmi_mip_APC 0.8752, n_indep_clades 2, frac_co_ZNF 0.990, passes_phylo_filter False, verdict 'ZNF clade artifact'.

findings.claim: Precomputed bundle sizes for a static-hosting portal are all small: significant enrichment rows (FDR<0.05) 25,750 rows / 4.58 MB CSV, or 6,331 rows / 1.11 MB if capped at top-20 per cluster; edge table (phylo-pass OR npmi>0.1) 7,210 rows / 0.74 MB; PWM bundle 0.56 MB JSON; positional histograms 84 KB JSON; member gene lists 537,356 pairs / 5.08 MB JSON.
findings.evidence: Written to /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/{enr_sig.csv, enr_sig_top20.csv, edges.csv} and measured with os.path.getsize; json.dumps length for the PWM bundle and gene lists.
findings.portal_relevance: Everything except the gene lists and full enrichment fits comfortably in a static bundle. Total for a fully client-side cluster view with top-20 terms: ~2.5 MB. Gene lists (5 MB) should be lazy-loaded per cluster or served from a small SQLite/parquet index.

gaps.gap: No sequence logo (PWM) for 434 of 900 clusters. STREME was only ever run on the 513 module-member clusters, and 62 of those (all protein) produced zero significant motifs. Cross-tab: 258 clusters have both a PWM and an auto-name; 229 clusters have NEITHER a PWM nor any FDR<0.05 term - those pages would show only counts and a positional histogram.
gaps.impact: Nearly half of all cluster detail pages have no visual motif identity, which is the single most expected element of a 'motif cluster' page. The gap is not random: it hits utr3 hardest (251 of 500 utr3 clusters were never run).
gaps.workaround: Run the existing pipeline on the 387 missing clusters. The STREME binary is present at /Users/wangyanz/software/meme/bin/streme and measured runtimes were 64.3 s (prot_0002, 976 seqs), 5.0 s (utr3_0001), 9.9 s (utr5_0006) - about 2.4 CPU-hours total, ~15 min at the pipeline's WORKERS=10. Reuse windows_fasta() and run_streme() from 16_consensus_repertoire.py verbatim so the new PWMs are identical in method to the 513 on disk. Expect ~100-150 protein clusters to still return nothing significant (prot_0002 already did); for those, fall back to the positional histogram plus a top-k-mer table. Do NOT fall back to stacking member strings: only 32 of 900 clusters have >=50% of members at the modal length.

gaps.gap: 437 of 900 clusters have no automatically derivable name (no term at FDR_cluster<0.05). The deficit is overwhelmingly on the RNA side: 377 of 500 utr3 and 57 of 100 utr5 clusters are unnamed, versus only 3 of 300 protein clusters.
gaps.impact: Cluster pickers, search results, network node labels and breadcrumbs would show bare ids like 'utr3_0342' for the majority of UTR clusters, making R2 navigation opaque exactly where the science is most novel.
gaps.workaround: Build a three-tier display name: (1) curated label from cluster_term_labels.csv for the 37 manuscript clusters; (2) top FDR<0.05 term from cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz for the 463; (3) for the rest, synthesise from what does exist - the top consensus string from consensus_meta.csv (451 clusters) plus a composition descriptor, e.g. 'utr3_0342 - CU-rich, 5-mer, n=330'. Compute the descriptor from base composition of member strings, which is available for all 900. Never leave a bare id.

gaps.gap: STREME sites.tsv cannot be mapped back to transcripts. The seq_ID column is an integer index into the discovery FASTA (headers are literally '>0', '>1', ...), and the FASTA was built from a motif_score-sorted, 1,200-capped subset of the cluster.
gaps.impact: The natural feature 'click a position in the logo, see the actual instances that support it' cannot be built from the cached STREME output. The per-motif site list is orphaned from gene identity.
gaps.workaround: Either (a) regenerate the discovery FASTA deterministically with windows_fasta() from 16_consensus_repertoire.py - same filter (motif_length>=5), same 1,200 cap, same sort by motif_score descending - and zip the resulting record order back onto sites.tsv seq_ID; or (b) skip sites.tsv entirely and re-scan all cluster instances against the PWM client-side or in the precompute (PWMs are tiny: max 5x4 or 15x20). Option (b) is preferable because it covers all instances, not just the capped 1,200, and produces a real per-instance match score.

gaps.gap: 282 of 600 UTR clusters and 99 of 300 protein clusters have ZERO protein/UTR partner passing the phylogenetic-independence filter, so R2's 'how does this motif interact with protein features' has no strict answer for them.
gaps.impact: Nearly half of UTR cluster pages hit an empty partner table at the manuscript's own threshold. Silently relaxing the threshold to fill the page would misrepresent the paper's central statistical claim.
gaps.workaround: Make the tier explicit in the UI. Default to passes_phylo_filter (2,620 edges), and when it is empty show a labelled empty state plus a one-click 'show suggestive associations (npmi_mip_APC > 0.1, not phylogenetically independent)' toggle - 7,210 edges, an exact superset since every passing pair has npmi_mip_APC > 0.1 (min 0.1001). Always render n_indep_clades and frac_co_ZNF next to any relaxed edge so the reader can see why it failed.

gaps.gap: 387 of 900 clusters have no module assignment, because modules.json / consensus_scope_clusters.csv only cover clusters participating in a within-module passing edge.
gaps.impact: R3's meta-module view can never link to 43% of clusters, and a cluster page reached from R1 (a highlighted motif on a transcript) will often have no module breadcrumb back to the network view.
gaps.workaround: Treat module membership as an optional badge, not a required field. For unassigned clusters, offer 'nearest module by best partner' computed from the top npmi_mip_APC partner's module - but label it as inferred, never as membership. Keep the R1 -> cluster -> module navigation resilient to a missing module.

gaps.gap: No cross-reference from the 1,226 discovered consensus strings to known RBP motif databases (CISBP-RNA, RBPmap, ATtRACT, Ray et al.) - nothing of the sort exists anywhere in the inspected trees.
gaps.impact: The portal cannot answer the first question a reader will ask of a UTR consensus: 'is UCUCC actually the PTBP motif?' The manuscript's own SRSF3/4 and PTBP claims are therefore not directly verifiable in the UI.
gaps.workaround: Use the eCLIP/PAR-CLIP/iCLIP enrichment already in cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz as the evidence proxy and label it honestly as 'RBPs whose CLIP peaks are enriched at this cluster's instances', not 'the RBP that binds this motif'. The per-cluster RBP tally supports this (utr3_0215 top: LARP4 18, PCBP1 15, PCBP2 14, DDX55 9, UPF1 8). If a real motif-database comparison is wanted later, TOMTOM ships with the same MEME install used for STREME and could compare the 0.56 MB PWM bundle against a downloaded RNA motif database.

gaps.gap: No stored alignment of motif instances within a cluster, and no per-instance PWM match score. The member strings are stored raw and are length-heterogeneous (median 37-45 distinct lengths per cluster).
gaps.impact: A 'view the aligned members' panel - the standard way to show what a cluster actually contains - has no backing data, and instances cannot be ranked by how well they match their own cluster's consensus.
gaps.workaround: In the precompute, slide each cluster's top PWM over each member string, keep the best-scoring window and its offset, and store (instance, offset, bits). This is the same computation coverage() in 16_consensus_repertoire.py already performs (COV_BITS=0.5 threshold, uniform background), so the definition would match the published coverage numbers. Output is one small table keyed on raw_motif_index.

gaps.gap: The enrichment table's display strings are not unique per cluster: 17,056 duplicated (cluster, display) groups, caused by MobiDB provenance keys (curated-phase_separation-{merge,priority,phasepdb,phasepro} all render as 'phase separation (curated)') and rare cross-source name collisions.
gaps.impact: The obvious 'top 3 enriched terms' query returns visibly repeated rows - this is not hypothetical, prot_0072 shows 'phase separation (curated)' three times in the top 3.
gaps.workaround: De-duplicate on (cluster, source, display) keeping the row with the smallest fdr_cluster, before ranking. (cluster, source, term) is verified unique, so the raw term string is the safe join key while display is the safe render key.

gaps.gap: No physical protein-RNA interaction evidence exists anywhere in the data. Every association is co-occurrence of motif clusters across genes (NPMI with APC correction plus a phylogenetic-recurrence filter), and the same is true of module membership.
gaps.impact: Every edge, every module and every 'interacts with' phrase in the UI risks being read as a demonstrated binding event - precisely the misreading the manuscript guards against.
gaps.workaround: Enforce the language at the schema level: name the edge field 'co-occurrence' in the data model so no template can accidentally emit 'binds'. Attach the concrete counter-example rather than a generic disclaimer: RAW_top30_annotated.csv already carries a verdict column with 25 'ZNF clade artifact', 4 'single-clade / weak', 1 'survives', including prot_0228 x utr5_0020 at npmi_raw 0.897 / frac_co_ZNF 0.990 / 2 clades that the filter correctly rejects. Show n_indep_clades and frac_co_ZNF on every edge, not behind a details toggle.

recommendations: Model the hierarchy explicitly in the portal's schema as four levels - instance (raw_motif_index) -> unique_motif_id (region + literal string) -> motif_cluster (region + kmeans label) -> module (513/900 only) - and make the contextual-embedding caveat a first-class UI element, not a footnote. 34,110 unique_motif_ids (85.9% of all multi-instance uids) land in 2 or more clusters, up to 176 for 'CTGGA'. Any page that implies 'this string belongs to this cluster' is wrong. On the R1 transcript view, every highlighted motif must carry its own row-level motif_cluster from the parquet; never look up a cluster from the string.

Build ONE precompute script that emits a static bundle, and run it before any UI work. Measured outputs: PWM bundle 0.56 MB JSON (451 clusters, 4 dp), positional histograms 84 KB (all 900), edges 0.74 MB (7,210 rows = phylo-pass OR npmi>0.1), enrichment top-20-per-cluster 1.11 MB (6,331 rows), cluster summary stats 900 rows. Total ~2.5 MB, which makes the entire R2 view client-side with no backend. Keep member gene lists (5.08 MB, 537,356 pairs) out of the bundle and lazy-load per cluster or serve from a small parquet/SQLite index.

Fill the STREME gap first - it is the highest-value 15 minutes in the project. 434 of 900 clusters currently have no logo and 229 have neither a logo nor a name. Measured cost to run the 387 never-run clusters is ~2.4 CPU-hours single-threaded and ~15 min at WORKERS=10, using windows_fasta()/run_streme() from 16_consensus_repertoire.py verbatim (streme --p <fa> --n <bg> --oc <dir> --nmotifs 12, plus --protein --minw 6 --maxw 15 or --rna --minw 5 --maxw 12). Do this before designing the cluster page, so the layout is built against real coverage rather than being retrofitted.

Never draw a logo by stacking member motif strings. Within-cluster lengths are heterogeneous - the median cluster has 37-45 distinct member lengths and only 21-25% of members share the modal length; just 32 of 900 clusters reach 50% at the mode. The STREME PWM is the only valid logo source. For clusters where STREME finds nothing significant (62 protein clusters already, plus whatever the 387 new runs return - prot_0002 returned 0), fall back to the positional histogram plus a top-k-mer composition table and say so on the page.

Give the cluster page two variants driven by region, not one generic template. Protein clusters get pLDDT distribution (300 clusters, medians 0.215-0.972 - a genuinely discriminating ordered-vs-IDR axis), InterPro/MobiDB/ELM/SignalP terms, and near-complete auto-naming (297/300). UTR clusters get no pLDDT, eCLIP/PAR-CLIP/iCLIP/miRNA evidence, and sparse naming (123/500 utr3, 43/100 utr5). A single template will show empty pLDDT panels on 600 pages and empty name slots on 434.

Implement the R2 partner table as two explicit tiers with the numbers on screen. STRICT = passes_phylo_filter (2,620 edges, 318/600 UTR clusters, median 5 partners, max 39) as the default; RELAXED = npmi_mip_APC > 0.1 (7,210 edges, 537/600 UTR clusters) behind a labelled toggle. These nest exactly: every passing pair has npmi_mip_APC > 0.1 (min 0.1001), n_indep_clades >= 8, co_count >= 10, frac_co_ZNF <= 0.40. Do not default to npmi > 0.05 - it lights up all 600 UTR clusters with a median of 33 partners and destroys the signal. For the 282 UTR clusters with no strict partner, show a deliberate empty state rather than silently relaxing.

Lead the UTR cluster page with the PROTEIN partner's features. 2,614 of 2,620 passing edges (99.8%) have a protein partner with at least one FDR<0.05 term, but only 1,180 (45.0%) have any RBP/miRNA term on the UTR side. The strong direction is UTR cluster -> partner protein clusters -> InterPro/MobiDB features; the cluster's own RBP annotation is supporting evidence. Verified worked examples to use as design targets: utr5_0004 -> prot_0040 (npmi 0.628, score 1.769, Histone-fold 26.5x), utr5_0079 -> prot_0072 (RNA-binding domain superfamily 11.1x, phase separation 9.3x), utr3_0215 -> prot_0038 (Ig-like domain superfamily 25.4x).

De-duplicate enrichment terms before rendering or the first screenshot will show a bug. (cluster, source, term) is unique but (cluster, display) is duplicated in 17,056 groups - prot_0072's top 3 are all 'phase separation (curated)' from four MobiDB provenance keys. Collapse on (cluster, source, display) keeping the smallest fdr_cluster, then rank. Join source=='InterPro' rows to interpro_entry_map.csv to make each chip a deep link with GO context.
